# An AI assistant that guides users inside your product

Aven works inside the applications you build. It answers contextual questions, identifies developer-registered pages and workflows, and lets your host application navigate and guide people to registered UI targets.

## Developer-declared context

Aven uses pages, elements, and workflows your team explicitly registers. The host application stays in control of navigation and UI behavior.

## Next step

Choose an SDK, register a real product task, and verify the target becomes available before guiding a user.

# Privacy Policy

Service provider: Himanshu Pathak, operating as Aven App Agent. Effective date: 18 October 2026.

## Scope and information processed

This policy covers the Aven website, dashboard, SDK integrations, knowledge assistants, and onboarding guides. We process account identifiers and contact details; app and workspace configuration; documents, URLs, and repository content you connect; questions and assistant responses; guide definitions; and usage, device, request, and security metadata. The information available depends on your integration and settings.

## How information is used [...] ## Your choices and security

You can manage connected sources and guides in your workspace and request access, correction, deletion, or account closure using the contact below. Available rights depend on applicable law. Browser storage supports authentication and product preferences. Aven uses access controls and managed infrastructure, but no storage or transmission system is completely secure.

## Website owners and the Chrome extension

If you integrate Aven into your website, you are responsible for informing users about that integration and obtaining any permission required for the data you send. The Aven Visual Onboarding Builder extension has a separate, more specific privacy policy at /privacy/aven-visual-builder. Contact us with privacy questions or concerns.

results.title: App review analysis with an AI agent (2026 guide) | AppReply
results.content:
App review analysis means turning what people write in App Store and Google Play reviews into decisions: what broke, since when, for whom, and what to fix first. An AI agent changes where you start. You skip the tagging and the report. You ask "why did our rating drop after the last release?" and get a chart back, with the reviews behind it.

The hard part is knowing whether to trust that chart. This guide covers what a trustworthy answer shows, works through three common questions, and ends with where replies come in. The examples use RADAR, the AI agent for app reviews in AppReply. The checks apply to any AI tool you point at your reviews.

## How app review analysis used to work [...] ## Three questions to ask this week

You don't need a new process to try this. Ask these three and hold each answer to the four checks:

 What changed this period, and why?
 Which topics are growing, and which reviews are behind them?
 What do reviewers of our closest rival complain about?

If an answer shows its chart, names its sample, opens onto its reviews and admits when the data is thin, you can take it into the product meeting. RADAR comes with every paid plan and the 10-day trial. See how the AI agent for app reviews works.

## Frequently asked questions

## What is app review analysis?

Turning what people write in App Store and Google Play reviews into decisions: what broke, since when, for which users, and what to fix first.

## How do you analyze app reviews with AI? [...] Ask two follow-ups every time. "Show me the reviews behind the drop" puts the words in front of you. "Is this the same complaint as last month?" separates a new bug from an old one that got louder. Already looking at the chart on the Ratings page? Click Point at content, pick the chart, and ask about it directly.

Once you know the cause, app store rating recovery covers what to do for each kind of drop.

## Question 2: is this complaint growing?

One loud week can pass for a trend. Count it over time:

> How have complaints about GPS accuracy, failed activity recordings and mobile data usage trended on Strava for Android, week by week?
